meta.title: Mermaid Syntax Cheat Sheet with Examples
meta.description: The mermaid syntax you actually use: node shapes, arrow types, subgraphs, styling and one working example per diagram type. Copy, paste, edit.

card.title: Mermaid syntax cheat sheet
card.excerpt: Node shapes, arrows, subgraphs and styling in one page — plus a working example of every diagram type mermaid renders.

intro: Mermaid has a large reference and a small subset that covers almost everything people draw. This page is that subset: shapes, arrows, grouping, colours, and one copy-paste example per diagram type. Every snippet below renders as-is — paste it into the [editor](app:) to see it.

blocks.text: The shortest diagram that works
A flowchart needs one declaration line and one arrow. `TD` means top-down; use `LR` for left-to-right, which suits wide processes better.

blocks.caption: A three-node flowchart, top to bottom.
blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A[Start] --> B{Ready?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Ship it]
  B -->|No| A

blocks.text: `A`, `B` and `C` are node ids — internal names, never drawn. The text in brackets is the label, and the bracket **style** is what picks the shape.
Node shapes
Shape is chosen by the delimiter pair around the label. These are the ones worth remembering:
Quote the label when it contains brackets, colons or quotes: `A["Load (raw) data"]`. Without quotes the parser sees your punctuation as syntax.
Arrows

rows: Arrow with a label on it

blocks.text: Arrow length is meaningful too: `-->` is one rank, `--->` pushes the target one rank further down. It is the simplest layout control mermaid gives you.
Grouping with subgraphs
A `subgraph` draws a labelled box around nodes. Subgraphs nest, and arrows may cross their borders freely.

blocks.caption: Two services, each with its own store.
blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  subgraph api["API"]
    H[Handler] --> S[(Postgres)]
  end
  subgraph worker["Worker"]
    Q[Queue] --> W[Job]
  end
  H --> Q

blocks.text: Colour and styling
`style` paints one node. `classDef` plus `class` paints a set of them, which is what you want past three or four nodes.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A[OK] --> B[Failed]
  style A fill:#16a34a,stroke:#333,color:#fff
  classDef bad fill:#dc2626,stroke:#333,color:#fff
  class B bad

blocks.text: Colours are part of the diagram source, so they survive export and travel with the file. Nothing here depends on a theme setting in the tool that renders it.
One example per diagram type
Sequence diagram

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant API
  participant DB
  User->>API: request
  API->>DB: query
  DB-->>API: rows
  API-->>User: response

blocks.text: Class diagram
State diagram

blocks.code:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Running: start
  Running --> Idle: stop
  Running --> [*]: finish

blocks.text: Entity relationship diagram

blocks.code:
erDiagram
  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
  CUSTOMER {
    string name
    string email
  }

blocks.text: Gantt chart

blocks.code:
gantt
  title Project
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  section Phase 1
  Task 1 :a1, 2026-01-01, 5d
  Task 2 :after a1, 5d

blocks.text: Where mermaid renders on its own

items: **GitHub** — a fenced ```mermaid block renders in issues, pull requests, comments and README files.
**GitLab** — the same fenced block, in issues, merge requests and the wiki.
**Notion** — a code block with the language set to Mermaid renders next to the source.
**Obsidian** — a fenced mermaid block renders in preview mode.
**Docs sites** — Docusaurus, MkDocs Material and VitePress all support mermaid blocks.

blocks.text: That is the real reason to keep diagrams as mermaid rather than as images: the diagram lives in the same text file as the thing it describes, and a code review can see what changed in it.

blocks.heading: Try any snippet on this page
blocks.text: Paste it into the code tab and it renders instantly — or build the same diagram on the canvas and read the syntax back.

items.q: How do I add a line break inside a node label?
items.a:
Use `
` inside a quoted label: `A["First line
Second line"]`. Mermaid renders the label as HTML, so the tag works even though the rest of the syntax is not HTML.

items.q: Why does my label break the diagram?
items.a: Almost always an unquoted bracket, parenthesis, colon or quote inside the label. Wrap the whole label in double quotes and the parser stops treating your punctuation as syntax.

Only indirectly. Pick the direction (`TD`, `LR`, `BT`, `RL`), use longer arrows (`--->`) to push nodes further apart, and group related nodes into subgraphs. Mermaid computes the rest — there are no coordinates.

items.q: Which mermaid version does this editor use?
items.a: Mermaid 11, the current major version, so everything documented for v10 and v11 syntax renders here.
